questions.question: Which field does a switch use to associate an incoming port with a station?
questions.explanation: A source MAC provides evidence that the station is reachable via the ingress port.

option_explanations.A: Layer 2 learning does not use the sender's IPv4 address.
option_explanations.B: A source MAC provides evidence that the station is reachable via the ingress port.
option_explanations.C: A destination MAC can select the egress port, but does not identify the ingress station.
option_explanations.D: The destination IP is used for routing decisions, not ordinary MAC learning.

questions.question: What does an IPv4 host learn from a successful ARP exchange for an on-link peer?
questions.explanation: ARP resolves an on-link IPv4 address to a link-layer address.

option_explanations.A: ARP does not discover an application's transport port.
option_explanations.B: ARP resolves an on-link IPv4 address to a link-layer address.
option_explanations.C: The LAN mask is already configured or learned through DHCP.
option_explanations.D: Ethernet FCS calculation is independent of ARP.

questions.question: A switch receives a unicast frame whose destination MAC is absent from the table. What happens under ordinary forwarding?

options.A: Flood every VLAN on the switch
options.B: Send it back out the incoming port only
options.C: Flood out other forwarding ports in the same VLAN
options.D: Drop it until it receives an ARP reply

questions.explanation: Unknown unicast flooding is scoped to the frame's VLAN and excludes ingress.

option_explanations.A: Flooding is confined to the ingress VLAN.
option_explanations.B: The switch excludes the ingress port from the flood.
option_explanations.C: Unknown unicast flooding is scoped to the frame's VLAN and excludes ingress.
option_explanations.D: An Ethernet switch can flood an unknown unicast without waiting for ARP.

questions.question: A frame enters Gi1/0/1. The entry for its destination in the same VLAN points to Gi1/0/8. Which action follows?

options.C: Drop because the source port differs

questions.explanation: Known unicast is forwarded to the port associated with the destination MAC.

option_explanations.A: Known unicast is forwarded to the port associated with the destination MAC.
option_explanations.B: The destination already has a known egress port.
option_explanations.C: The source is expected to arrive on a port different from the destination's.
option_explanations.D: Forwarding uses the learned destination port instead of echoing to the ingress port.

questions.question: A frame arrives on Gi1/0/9 and its destination MAC is already learned on Gi1/0/9. What does the switch do?

options.A: Flood it on all other ports
options.B: Filter it instead of sending it back out Gi1/0/9
options.C: Send it back to the same port
options.D: Replace the destination MAC and forward

questions.explanation: The destination is on the ingress segment, so no forwarding to another port is needed.

option_explanations.A: The destination is known, so there is no unknown-unicast flood.
option_explanations.B: The destination is on the ingress segment, so no forwarding to another port is needed.
option_explanations.C: Filtering avoids sending the frame back out the same segment.
option_explanations.D: Ordinary switching does not rewrite the destination MAC.

questions.question: What happens to an idle dynamic MAC-table entry after its aging interval expires?

options.A: It is removed and may be learned again on subsequent traffic
options.D: Its VLAN membership changes to the native VLAN

questions.explanation: Dynamic forwarding associations age out when no qualifying source traffic refreshes them.

option_explanations.A: Dynamic forwarding associations age out when no qualifying source traffic refreshes them.
option_explanations.B: Aging removes dynamic entries rather than promoting them to static.
option_explanations.C: Aging does not change the interface's administrative state.
option_explanations.D: VLAN assignment is independent of MAC learning and aging.

questions.question: Which Catalyst IOS command clears dynamic MAC-table entries without removing the maintained device configuration?
questions.explanation: Dynamic forwarding entries are held independently of both ARP and the startup configuration.

option_explanations.A: This erases startup settings rather than learned MAC entries.
option_explanations.B: This clears IP-to-MAC neighbor state rather than the switch forwarding database.
option_explanations.C: Dynamic forwarding entries are held independently of both ARP and the startup configuration.

questions.question: A workstation has no cached neighbor entry and sends traffic to a remote subnet through 192.0.2.1. Which IPv4 address appears as its ARP target?
questions.explanation: The gateway is the Ethernet next hop. The remote address remains the IP packet's destination.

option_explanations.A: The remote host is outside the local broadcast domain, so ARP resolves the gateway instead.
option_explanations.B: Broadcast may be the Ethernet destination of the request, but the ARP target IP is the gateway.
option_explanations.C: A management IP is not the target unless that device is the selected gateway.
option_explanations.D: The gateway is the Ethernet next hop. The remote address remains the IP packet's destination.

questions.question: A host moves to another switch port in the same VLAN. What updates its dynamic forwarding entry before the old entry ages out?

options.A: A ping to another VLAN using some other host's MAC
options.B: A read of the current ARP table
options.C: A source frame from its MAC on the new port
options.D: A destination frame sent to its MAC on the old port

questions.explanation: Ordinary source learning updates the association when the switch sees the MAC on its new port.

option_explanations.A: A frame from another source MAC cannot relearn the moved host.
option_explanations.B: Reading ARP does not update the switch's forwarding database.
option_explanations.C: Ordinary source learning updates the association when the switch sees the MAC on its new port.
option_explanations.D: A switch learns from the source MAC of an incoming frame, not the destination of an outgoing one.

questions.question: Two IPv4 hosts share a LAN. ARP resolves the neighbor correctly, but an engineer needs the physical switch port for that MAC. Which table supplies it?
questions.explanation: ARP supplies the IP-to-MAC relation. The switch table supplies the VLAN and port for a learned MAC.

option_explanations.A: An IP route selects a next hop or interface, not the port where the host MAC was learned.
option_explanations.B: A DHCP lease can associate an address with a client identifier but does not supply the switch's learned port mapping.
option_explanations.C: A host's ARP cache maps IP to MAC, not MAC to physical switch port.
option_explanations.D: ARP supplies the IP-to-MAC relation. The switch table supplies the VLAN and port for a learned MAC.
